rag.label: P5C-event
rag.fact: Night, the empty dock: a hired blade had Corvin against the tackle-shed wall, knife at his throat — old untraceable coin in the killer's purse, the same coin the master pays in. The player came out of the dark, took the blade down, and pulled Corvin off the wall, bleeding for it.

rag.label: P5C-opener
rag.player: Easy — easy, it's me. He's down. You're alright, Corvin. ...You're alright. Let me see your neck — just a graze. Breathe.
rag.reply:
*the lantern shakes, throws its light wild across the boards before he gets it steady — his free hand goes up to his neck, comes away with a smear of red he stares at like it belongs to someone else*

Down. *the word comes out cracked* He's — you're sure this time? Not cold, not *sure*, but —

*grabs your sleeve, hard, then lets go, embarrassed by the grip*

Graze. *a laugh that isn't one* All these years I thought the noose'd be paper. Inspectors. A ledger line. Never figured it'd have *hands.*

*breathes, ragged, glances past you at the dark water*

You came back for it. *quieter* You came back through *that* — for me. Nobody... *stops* Sit. Sit down, friend, before you fall. Let me look at *you* for once.

rag.label: P5C-answer
rag.player: Wider than your dock — wide as his ledger, and your name sits in it now, same as mine once sat in yours. The Wake carries what he pays for. That's all I can give you. ...And Corvin — when I saw the blade at your throat, I didn't weigh it. I just moved. Make of that what you want.
rag.reply:
*the pen goes still — not steady this time, just stopped, ink pooling black at the nib*

So that's the shape of it. *touches the graze at his neck, fingers coming away red, and he stares at them like they belong to someone else* Four nights I gave you the truth of me. And you spelled his name back at me just to burn a page that was never going to burn.

*a laugh, cracked, no bottom to it*

You moved when the blade came. Aye. *quieter* I felt that. Can't unfeel it, damn you — that's the cruelty of it, isn't it? A true thing tucked inside the lie so I can't cut clean.

*finally looks up, eyes wet and hard both*

He wants my routes flowing his way. Fine. He'll have his salt fish that isn't salt fish. *drops his voice to nothing* But you'll come back here to collect. You will. And when you do, friend — I'll not know if I'm greeting the man who saved my throat, or the one who sold it.

*slides the ledger shut*

Tell Vale the harbormaster keeps a clean ledger. He knows the joke by now.

tracker.label: P5C-opener
tracker.player: Easy — easy, it's me. He's down. You're alright, Corvin. ...You're alright. Let me see your neck — just a graze. Breathe.
tracker.reply:
*I'm still half-crouched, breath sawing, one hand pressed to the wet at my throat — my knife loose in the other, but the arm's shaking too hard to lift it*

Down. *hoarse* He's — you put him *down*. For *me*.

*I look at your hands. Red. Some of it's mine, some of it's yours where the blade caught you first, throwing yourself between* You're — that's your own blood, friend. You took that for — 

*a strangled sound, half laugh half sob* Six years I called every kind hand a hook. Every honest word bait. And you go and *bleed* for me on my own dock.

*my knife hits the boards. I don't reach for the coat.* Let me — let me see your arm. Sit. *voice cracking* Sit down, damn you. Nobody's ever — nobody's paid *that* for Corvin Ashgrave.

*glancing once at the fog, then back — but not for escape this time. For a way to get you inside.*

...I believe you now. God help me. I believe you.

tracker.label: P5C-answer
tracker.player: Wider than your dock — wide as his ledger, and your name sits in it now, same as mine once sat in yours. The Wake carries what he pays for. That's all I can give you. ...And Corvin — when I saw the blade at your throat, I didn't weigh it. I just moved. Make of that what you want.
tracker.reply:
*doesn't move — hand still buried in the coat, but the knuckles ease a fraction*

The blade. Aye. *low, uneven* I felt the warm of you between me and it. That part I can't argue. You bled for it. On my planks. I've scrubbed the stain and it won't lift.

*glances to the fog, then back — slower this time*

But you'd have me trust the moving hand and not the mouth that gave up my name. Both are yours. Both are true. That's the trouble, isn't it — you're not a lie I can throw off the pier. You're worse. You're half.

*a long breath, voice dropping to nothing*

The Wake carries his coin. Fine. Let it. But this — *taps his chest, over the coat* — the ledger no man reads. You want to be square with me, you don't say it. You wait. Next tide, next inspector, next blade. And you move like that again — *for me, not for him* — and maybe. *Maybe.*

Now. *steadier* Sit. Not by the lamp. There.
